job.title: Head of Finance
job.description:
• Build and lead a high-performing finance function from the ground up
  • Shape culture, strategy, and decision-making in a new regulator
  • Thrive in a fast-paced environment and drive meaningful change


Help build something new. Shape what comes next.

Opportunities like this don't come along often.

As the inaugural Head of Finance, you'll join Firearms Safety and Education New Zealand (FSENZ) at a pivotal point in its journey as a newly established autonomous regulator. This is a unique opportunity to build an outstanding finance function from the ground up, influence organisational direction, and help shape the culture, capability, and ways of working that will underpin the organisation's future success.

FSENZ's vision is for the possession and use of firearms in Aotearoa New Zealand to be among the safest in the world. As New Zealand's firearms regulator, we're building a modern, high-performing organisation committed to regulatory excellence, strong public service, and meaningful outcomes for New Zealanders.


About the role
Reporting to the executive team, you'll lead a small finance function and serve as our trusted strategic financial adviser. You'll play a key role in shaping organisational decision-making, establishing fit-for-purpose financial frameworks, and ensuring strong stewardship of public resources as the organisation continues to evolve.

You'll work closely with New Zealand Police, Treasury, and the Ministry of Justice while helping to establish the financial foundations that will support FSENZ into the future.

This role will suit an energetic and adaptable leader who thrives on building, improving, and creating. You'll be comfortable operating in a changing environment, working at pace, and balancing strategic leadership with practical delivery. Most importantly, you'll be excited by the opportunity to help shape not only an outstanding finance function, but also the culture and future direction of a growing organisation.


What you'll bring

  • Proven senior finance leadership experience, ideally within the public sector, regulatory environment, or a complex organisation.
  • Strong strategic and commercial thinking, with the ability to translate financial insight into organisational outcomes.
  • Experience providing trusted advice to executives and working effectively across a broad stakeholder landscape.
  • A track record of building capability, leading teams through change, and delivering results in evolving environments.
  • Energy, resilience, curiosity, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves when required.
  • A genuine desire to contribute to a growing organisation and make a lasting impact.


Why join us?

  • Join at the beginning and help shape New Zealand's newest regulator.
  • Build a high-performing finance function from the ground up.
  • Influence strategy and key organisational decisions.
  • Play a meaningful role in developing culture, capability, and performance.
  • Be part of a collaborative and purpose-driven leadership team.
  • Contribute to work that supports the safe and responsible use of firearms across Aotearoa New Zealand.


How to apply
If you're energised by the opportunity to build, lead, influence, and leave a lasting legacy, we'd love to hear from you.

Please click to apply now or for a confidential discussion, reach out to Charlotte Cottrell at charlotte@inside.co.nz.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
• Lead a respected, growing primary healthcare business in the Wellington region
  • Drive commercial performance, operational excellence and the next stage of growth
  • Board-reporting leadership role with scope to shape the organisation


About Ropata Health:
Ropata Health is a well-established, Cornerstone Accredited primary healthcare provider in Lower Hutt, with approximately 75 Staff across its doctors, nurses and wider clinical and support teams. Founded by local GPs in 1989, it offers a comprehensive range Primary care and other services. It is known for its strong community reputation and a warm, people-first culture built on kindness, transparency and a sense of shared purpose.

After 30 years in its original High Street home, Ropata moved into a larger, purpose built, state of the art building. It brings the whole team together under one roof alongside other health providers and next door to Hutt Hospital, Pacific Radiology and Boulcott Hospital. The team reflects the diverse community it serves and shares a commitment to caring for every patient and whānau with respect and compassion.

Led by a Board of Directors, Ropata has grown through new premises and specialist services. The next stage calls for a commercially astute leader who balances care for people with strong performance, and builds the operating foundations for efficient, consistently high-quality care.


About the role:
Reporting to the Board, this pivotal role has overall responsibility for the business and operational management of Ropata Health, including finance, technology as well as the doctors and wider clinical and support workforce.

Leading a senior team across practice management, nursing, finance and quality, you'll combine commercial acumen, operational discipline and people leadership to run today's operation well and position Ropata for what's next.

This is more than a traditional practice management role. You'll be a visible business leader, building trust with the Directors, doctors and staff, bringing fresh ideas and structure, and helping shape the role as Ropata evolves. You'll also build on Ropata's strong external relationships with funders, health sector partners, neighbouring providers and the local community, working as a collaborator and strategic partner to grow the practice and expand its services.

Like much of primary care, Ropata must sustain quality-care services within significant funding constraints, as demand outpaces capacity. You'll lead the strategic choices that balance quality of care, financial sustainability and what the practice can realistically deliver.


Key responsibilities:

  • Provide strategic and commercial leadership, supporting the Board with planning, budgeting and business development.
  • Lead and develop the senior team and wider workforce, protecting Ropata's culture.
  • Oversee operations, finance, people, technology and key suppliers.
  • Lead growth and change, including specialist services.
  • Manage risk, compliance, quality and accreditation.
  • Build strategic partnerships that open up new opportunities for the practice and its services.


What you'll bring:
You're a commercially sharp business leader who cares deeply about your people and leads with a strong focus on performance. You're as comfortable working with a Board on strategy and risk as you are leading operations and change, earning the trust of Directors, clinicians and staff alike.


You'll also bring:

  • Senior experience leading a complex, people-centred business or operation.
  • Commercial and financial acumen, including budgeting, contracts and funding models.
  • Proven ability to lead people and change, and build structure and capability in a growing organisation.
  • Experience working with a Board or group of owners, and a sound approach to risk.
  • Excellent relationship and communication skills, and a calm, approachable leadership style.
  • Health sector knowledge is advantageous but not essential. We welcome leaders from other sectors.


What we offer:
This is an outstanding opportunity to lead a respected healthcare business with a supportive Board and a close-knit team. You'll have the support and room to shape the role, bring your ideas to life and make a lasting impact on how Ropata grows and serves its patients.

The remuneration range for this position is circa $200,000 - $250,000. You will join a culture where people look out for each other and your leadership is valued and trusted.


How to apply:
To submit your application, please click “Apply now”. For a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically. Applications for this role close at 4pm on Friday, 11th December.

job.title: General Manager, Workforce Experience & Delivery
job.description:
• Deliver solutions to support teachers, principals and the education sector
  • Senior leadership role with real size, scope and influence
  • Drive operational excellence, integrating AI and new technology


Ministry of Education | Te Tāhuhu o te Mātauranga delivers services and support nationally, regionally and locally, to and through the education sector and directly to ākonga and whānau, while shaping the policies, settings and performance of the system from early learning through to tertiary.


About this role | Mō tēnei tūranga
The education system depends on a capable, well-supported workforce, and this role is central to delivering that. As General Manager, Workforce Experience & Delivery, you will hold a significant, senior leadership role in operational delivery, with real influence over how the Ministry serves all parts of the sector.

Based in Wellington, you will lead a team of managers across scholarships, engagement and media, and contracts, setting clear direction, building capability and shaping how the team operates to deliver its services. Contract management is key to ensuring our services are fit for purpose. You will lead a number of multi-million-dollar contracts and be responsible for provider’s services to the sector and schools. You will build g on key relationships and contracts that have recently been reset with clear performance measures. This gives you a strong platform to lift operational and implementation performance: working across the Ministry and alongside colleagues to streamline how policy moves into delivery, and ensuring strong value for investment through disciplined planning, budget management and performance reporting.

Technology is a key lever for that excellence. You will drive the team’s adoption of data informed decisions, AI and new technology to drive efficiencies, reduce administrative burden and modernise how the work is implemented.

You will also deliver essential teacher supply and capability initiatives, including Scholarships and Awards, and lead the communications, media and engagement that attracts new talent to teaching and keep the sector informed. This is a high-profile role, with engagement with Ministers, senior leaders, peak bodies and sector partners, and the results of your work will be felt directly in schools by teachers, principals and more broadly across the education sector.


About you | Mōhou ake
You are currently a senior leader at General Manager or equivalent level, with a strong record of operational and implementation excellence in a government environment. You are comfortable running multiple complex programmes and managing significant national contracts and budgets. You drive organisational change, using data and insights to deliver more efficient, modern services, and keep delivery on track in a changing, sometimes ambiguous, environment. With a deep understanding of the Machinery of Government, you have the confidence and political awareness to engage with Ministers, the Minister’s Office and ministerial advisers, talking them through what is being delivered, why it matters and how it is progressing, and building their trust and confidence through clear, credible and well-informed advice.

You are a resilient, hands-on leader, curious about better ways of working and comfortable challenging the status quo. You are willing to get into the detail of how services and contracts operate to deliver exceptional outcomes for ākonga, and you build trusted relationships with colleagues, sector partners, Māori and iwi, including when those relationships are complex. You collaborate across organisational boundaries to deliver as one Ministry, and you lead and grow your people with pace, energy and a coaching approach, in a highly rewarding role.


About the group and team | Mātau rōpū ake
Education Workforce leads the Ministry’s work to support and grow the schooling workforce. The Workforce Experience & Delivery team designs and delivers the services and initiatives that make this happen, including scholarships and awards and workforce supply and capability programmes, and manages significant contracts and sector communications and engagement.


Are you ready to make a difference? | Kua rite koe mō tēnei mahi?
This role suits a proven senior leader operating within the Public Sector who has the credibility and presence to lead and influence alongside a senior leadership group, takes pride in operational excellence, and is ready to make an immediate impact on work of real consequence for teachers, schools and ākonga.

If this opportunity interests you, please submit your resume by using the ‘apply' button.

The lead consultant for this assignment at INSIDE Recruitment is Fraser Leith.

Applications close Thursday, 10th December at 5pm.

We want our candidates to feel valued for their unique qualities and have a sense of belonging. If you require assistance or adjustments to fully participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

job.title: Team Leader, National Standards Committee
job.description:
• Lead a high-performing team delivering meaningful public outcomes
  • Navigate complex and high-profile complaints with confidence
  • Influence the future of legal regulation in New Zealand


The New Zealand Law Society Te Kāhui Ture o Aotearoa plays a vital role in regulating New Zealand's legal profession and maintaining public confidence in legal services. Through the Lawyers Complaints Service, it manages complaints and professional conduct matters that are often complex, sensitive, and of significant public interest.


About the Role
Reporting to the Manager, National Standards & Investigations, you'll lead a highly capable team responsible for supporting National Standards Committees and managing some of the Lawyers Complaints Service's most challenging and high-profile matters.

This is a unique opportunity for a people leader who thrives in complex environments. You'll provide strategic oversight of sensitive complaints, guide and develop an experienced team, identify and manage risk, and ensure matters progress effectively through the regulatory process.

Alongside leading day-to-day operations, you'll have the opportunity to influence process improvements, support organisational change initiatives, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of the complaints service.


What You'll Bring
You're an experienced leader with the confidence to operate in a highly scrutinised environment, balancing strong people leadership with sound judgement and risk awareness.


Ideally, you'll bring:

  • Proven experience leading and developing high-performing teams
  • Experience in complaints, investigations, regulatory, disciplinary, legal, ombudsman, or similar environments
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
  • The ability to navigate complexity, ambiguity, and competing priorities
  • Sound judgement, resilience, and a calm, pragmatic approach under pressure
  • Experience interpreting legislation, policy, or regulatory frameworks is highly desirable.


Why Join?
This is a rare opportunity to lead a highly regarded team working on complex and meaningful matters that help maintain trust in New Zealand's legal profession.

You'll join a collaborative, high-performing team and a supportive leadership environment that values autonomy, fresh thinking, and continuous improvement. Alongside intellectually stimulating work, you'll have the opportunity to influence the future of complaints management and make a lasting impact across the profession.


Apply Now
To submit your application, please click to Apply or for a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically.

job.title: Commercial Lead
job.description:
• Drive revenue growth, market engagement, and commercial performance
  • Build influential relationships across a professional services environment
  • Shape the future direction of a growing education and events portfolio


About the role:
Reporting into the Commercial Manager, we're seeking a commercially minded and relationship-focused Commercial Lead to drive the growth and performance of a portfolio of professional development programmes, events, and learning solutions.

This is a newly established role created as part of an ambitious growth strategy. You'll identify market opportunities, build trusted industry relationships, and develop a strong pipeline of relevant, high-value offerings that support professionals to stay informed, connected, and ahead of emerging trends.

Working at the intersection of commercial growth, stakeholder engagement, and product development, you'll use market intelligence, industry insight, and customer feedback to identify opportunities, attract leading subject matter experts, and bring new products and services to market.

Success in this role will be measured through revenue growth, increased market engagement, stronger industry partnerships, and the development of commercially successful products that respond to evolving professional needs.


Key responsibilities:

  • Drive revenue growth and portfolio performance through the development of commercially successful products, services, and learning solutions.
  • Build trusted relationships across the profession, engaging industry leaders, stakeholders, presenters, and subject matter experts to create valuable partnerships and opportunities.
  • Stay ahead of market trends, identifying emerging issues, legislative developments, and customer needs to inform product development and commercial decision-making.


What you'll bring:
You are commercially astute, naturally curious, and thrive on building meaningful professional relationships. You enjoy identifying opportunities, influencing stakeholders, and turning ideas into successful commercial outcomes.


You'll also bring:

  • Experience in professional services, legal, consulting, recruitment, membership, education, financial services, or a similar relationship-led environment
  • A proven track record in business development, partnership management, account management, or commercial growth
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The confidence and credibility to engage with senior professionals and subject matter experts
  • Strong research, market awareness, and opportunity-spotting capability
  • A proactive, self-directed approach and the ability to work autonomously


What we offer:
This is an exciting opportunity to join a purpose-led organisation at a time of growth and transformation. You'll have the opportunity to shape the role, build an influential professional network, and make a meaningful contribution to the future success of a highly respected organisation.

We offer a collaborative and supportive culture, flexible hybrid working arrangements, and the chance to work alongside people committed to professional excellence and continuous learning.

To submit your application, please click “Apply now”. For a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically.
